scope.title: Scope
scope.body: Applies to pronuxfin.com and PRONUXFIN-operated subdomains, including authenticated areas (dashboard, simulated portfolio, alerts, and tools).

dataCollected.title: Data we collect

usage.title: Purposes

sharing.title: Sharing

HomeFaq.title: Clarity before you start
HomeFaq.description: Straight answers on live data, regulatory limits, and what PRONUXFIN is — and is not.

live.q: Are quotes on the home page and market desk live?
live.a: When BRAPI_TOKEN and upstreams respond, the desk shows recent readings with freshness badges. On failure or demo mode, the UI states it explicitly — no fictional numbers posing as market data.

advice.q: Does PRONUXFIN recommend buying or selling assets?
advice.a: No. We provide reading infrastructure, educational projection, and cognitive organization. Projections and AI structure hypotheses; suitability and decisions are yours alone.

sources.q: Where does public data come from?
sources.a: Brazilian equities via BRAPI, crypto in BRL via CoinGecko, macro and calendar via Financial Modeling Prep when configured, news via RSS with visible sources. Each block shows provider and state (live, partial, or unavailable).

account.q: Do I need an account for the market desk and news?
account.a: Not for the public market layer, news, and open tools. The private desk (portfolio, alerts, dossier) requires sign-up with the same visual standard and security limits.

ai.q: How does AI fit the desk?
ai.a: As an evidence and workflow organizer — not an oracle. Answers reference available context; when data is missing, the UI says so. You validate before acting.

juros-compostos-guia.title: How to calculate compound interest in practice
juros-compostos-guia.description: Understand compounding logic, monthly contributions and realistic simulations — without return promises.
juros-compostos-guia.toolCtaLead: Use the free calculator to test initial capital, contributions and annual rate.

sections.heading: Why compound interest is powerful
paragraphs: With simple interest, returns apply only to the original principal. With compounding, each period earns on what was already accumulated — long charts curve upward when rates are positive.
Investors use this to model pensions, liquid fixed-income reserves and financial independence goals.

sections.heading: Steps to build a simulation
paragraphs: Set a realistic initial amount — zero is fine if you're starting out. Enter monthly contributions that fit your budget.
Pick a rate aligned with the product modeled: CDI for daily liquidity, inflation-linked for long horizons, or a conservative band for diversified portfolios.
Compare 5, 10 and 20 year horizons. Small rate or contribution changes materially affect final wealth.

sections.heading: Limits of any simulation
paragraphs: Calculators don't predict crises, tax rule changes or behavior. Inflation, taxes and fees reduce net returns.
Use simulations for education and planning — not as guaranteed future wealth.

what.a: Simple interest doesn't stack on principal. Compound interest does — most relevant over long horizons.

how.a: When income, goals or risk profile change — or after major macro events. Not necessarily every month.

risk.a: No. It's a math hypothesis. Real markets fluctuate and products carry distinct risks.

cdi-selic-ipca.title: CDI, Selic and IPCA: differences every investor should know
cdi-selic-ipca.description: Three acronyms on every fixed-income statement. Know each role before comparing products.
cdi-selic-ipca.toolCtaLead: Simulate how monthly contributions perform at different rates.

sections.heading: Selic: the benchmark policy rate
paragraphs: Selic is set at COPOM meetings and influences credit costs and post-fixed public bond yields.
When Selic rises, post-fixed fixed income often looks relatively more attractive — but tenor and liquidity matter as much as rate.

sections.heading: CDI: interbank reference
paragraphs: CDI tracks Selic closely and benchmarks DI funds, CDBs and many bank products.
“100% of CDI” means roughly replicating that reference before taxes and fees.

sections.heading: IPCA: official inflation
paragraphs: IPCA measures Brazilian consumer inflation. Inflation targets guide Central Bank decisions.
Comparing only “% per year” across prefixed, post-fixed and inflation-linked products can distort the picture. Always check tenor, liquidity, credit risk and tax.

what.q: Are CDI and Selic the same?
what.a: Not identical, but they move together. Many investors use CDI as a proxy for short post-fixed fixed income.

how.q: Should I only pick CDI-linked products?
how.a: Depends on goal and horizon. Emergency funds need liquidity; retirement may mix inflation-linked and other assets — ideally with a licensed professional.

risk.a: High IPCA erodes idle cash. Inflation-linked holders partly offset via indexing — but allocation matters.

copom-e-investimentos.title: COPOM and investments: what moves when Selic shifts
copom-e-investimentos.description: Central Bank meetings affect credit, fixed income and equity mood. Know what to watch without impulse reactions.
copom-e-investimentos.toolCtaLead: Check COPOM dates and other macro events on the calendar.

sections.heading: What COPOM is
paragraphs: The Monetary Policy Committee sets Selic target at periodic meetings. Statements and minutes signal views on inflation, jobs and credit.
Investors watch COPOM because rates directly affect public bonds, loans and indirectly equities and FX.

sections.heading: Typical fixed income & equity effects
paragraphs: Higher Selic often favors post-fixed bonds relatively and can reduce risk appetite at times. Lower Selic may improve backdrop for volatile assets — but sectors diverge.
No mechanical reaction: global context, fiscal policy and earnings also matter.

sections.heading: Prepare without guessing the outcome
paragraphs: Use the macro calendar for high-impact dates. Avoid over-concentrating on one rate scenario.
Long-term plans rarely should pivot on a single meeting — unless your financial life changed structurally.

what.a: The Central Bank publishes an annual calendar. PRONUXFIN shows these on the macro agenda when the source is available.

how.q: Should I sell stocks before COPOM?
how.a: PRONUXFIN doesn't recommend trades. Many long-term investors observe volatility without changing plan for one event.

risk.a: Post-fixed bonds tend to reflect rate expectations. Markets price part of moves before the official statement.

cdi.summary: Interbank rate used as fixed-income benchmark.
cdi.metaDescription: CDI meaning, relation to Selic and why it appears on CDBs and DI funds.
cdi.definition: Certificado de Depósito Interbancário (CDI) is an interbank lending rate close to Selic. Brazilian investors use it to benchmark post-fixed fixed income.
cdi.example: A CDB at “102% of CDI” aims to pay slightly above that reference before tax.

selic.summary: Brazil's benchmark interest rate set by COPOM.
selic.metaDescription: Selic definition, COPOM role and impact on investments and credit.
selic.definition: Selic is Brazil's monetary policy target rate set by the Central Bank at COPOM meetings.
selic.example: Tesouro Selic and post-fixed CDBs tend to follow Selic moves over time.

ipca.metaDescription: What IPCA measures and why investors use IPCA+ bonds for long goals.
ipca.definition: IPCA measures official Brazilian consumer inflation and informs Central Bank targets.
ipca.example: Tesouro IPCA+ pays a real rate above IPCA-measured inflation.

ticker.summary: Trading symbol for a stock or ETF.
ticker.metaDescription: Ticker meaning on B3 — how to read symbols like PETR4 or VALE3.
ticker.definition: A ticker is the short symbol identifying a listed asset — e.g. PETR4 for Petrobras ordinary shares on B3.
ticker.example: Numeric suffix indicates share class per B3 rules.

dividend-yield.metaDescription: How to calculate dividend yield and limits of the metric.
dividend-yield.definition: Dividend yield is dividends paid (or expected) divided by current price, as a percentage.
dividend-yield.example: A R$50 stock paying R$2.50 in dividends implies ~5% yield — simplified.

pe-ratio.summary: Price divided by earnings per share.
pe-ratio.metaDescription: Price/earnings meaning and how investors use it in equity analysis.
pe-ratio.definition: Price/Earnings compares market price to earnings per share. High multiples may reflect growth expectations — or overpricing, depending on context.
pe-ratio.example: P/E of 15x means the market pays 15 times annual EPS — compare peers and history.

copom.summary: Committee that sets Selic in Brazil.
copom.metaDescription: COPOM role, meeting calendar and link to investments.
copom.definition: Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee sets the Selic target and publishes inflation guidance.
copom.example: COPOM meetings appear on PRONUXFIN's calendar as high-impact events.

tesouro-selic.summary: Post-fixed government bond linked to Selic.
tesouro-selic.metaDescription: Tesouro Selic features, liquidity and emergency-fund use.
tesouro-selic.definition: Tesouro Selic is a Brazilian government bond yielding roughly Selic. Often cited for emergency reserves after initial grace.
tesouro-selic.example: Don't confuse with IPCA+ or prefixed Tesouro — risk/return profiles differ.

poupanca.summary: Regulated savings with its own yield rules.
poupanca.metaDescription: Basic poupança yield rules vs other liquid products.
poupanca.definition: Brazilian caderneta de poupança pays under legal rules tied to Selic and deposit anniversary. Simple but not always the most efficient reserve.
poupanca.example: With high Selic, liquid CDBs or Tesouro Selic may yield more — consider tax and profile.

renda-fixa.summary: Investments with more predictable return rules.
renda-fixa.metaDescription: Fixed income definition, examples (CDB, Tesouro) vs variable income.
renda-fixa.definition: Fixed income covers instruments with remuneration set by rules or indexers — CDI, Selic, IPCA or prefixed rates. Credit, liquidity and inflation risks remain.
renda-fixa.example: CDB, LCI, LCA and Tesouro Direto are common in Brazil.

renda-variavel.summary: Assets whose market price fluctuates — stocks, REITs, ETFs.
renda-variavel.metaDescription: Variable income meaning, risks and relation to B3 equities.
renda-variavel.definition: Variable income includes listed assets without contractually fixed returns — stocks, FIIs, BDRs, ETFs. Volatility can be high.
renda-variavel.example: Buying PETR4 exposes you to market price — unlike a CDB with a coupon rule.

aporte.summary: New money added to investments or simulations.
aporte.metaDescription: Monthly contribution definition and compounding impact.
aporte.definition: Aporte is additional money invested periodically. In PRONUXFIN simulators, steady monthly contributions often matter more than timing the market.
aporte.example: Contributing R$500/month in the compound calculator shows cumulative effect over years.

AboutPage.heroTitle: We started with a dream: make the financial desk accessible, clear, and trustworthy
AboutPage.heroLead: PRONUXFIN didn't begin as another quotes app. It began with the conviction that anyone who invests, studies, or stewards their own wealth deserves the same clarity large desks have — without opaque barriers, noise, or empty promises.
AboutPage.originTitle: A dream before it was a product
AboutPage.originLead: Behind the platform is a simple, stubborn idea.
AboutPage.originBody: We saw smart people making important financial decisions with fragmented tools: quotes in one place, news elsewhere, loose spreadsheets, and generic AI with no context. The market doesn't wait — but information arrived late, confused, or without a source.
AboutPage.originBody2: PRONUXFIN was born to unite live markets, wealth projection, a news radar, and assisted intelligence on one cognitive desk. Not to replace your judgment, but to give back time, method, and transparency to those who take finance seriously.
AboutPage.journeyTitle: From concept to the desk you use today
AboutPage.journeyLead: We built in layers — infrastructure first, experience second, always with engineering ethics.

timeline.title: The dream of one desk
timeline.description: We defined that markets, personal finance, and education shouldn't live in silos. The goal was a Brazilian platform with a global view, institutional language, and accessibility for everyone.

timeline.title: Infrastructure with discipline

pillars.title: Clarity over hype
pillars.description: Data with sources, explicit limits, and language that respects your intelligence. We never sell certainty where only probability exists.

pillars.title: Security by design
pillars.description: Revocable sessions, WebAuthn, rate limits, CSP, and continuous audit. Protecting your digital wealth is part of the product, not an appendix.

pillars.title: Real financial education

pillars.title: Brazil at the center, the world on the horizon

AssetTerminal.metaDescription: Private asset dossier for {symbol} on PRONUXFIN: session, dividends, returns, ratios, statements, risk and related news.
AssetTerminal.signalContextLinked: Related news already connected to the asset
AssetTerminal.signalContextBuilding: Editorial coverage still expanding for this asset
AssetTerminal.chartSubtitle: Up to roughly ten years of daily sessions when the upstream feed allows; derived annual metrics use the same window.
AssetTerminal.profileSubtitle: Corporate identity, headquarters, IPO and editorial coverage — the institutional layer of the dossier.
AssetTerminal.profileCoverage: Current coverage combines market snapshot, history and PRONUXFIN curation. Main source: {source}.
AssetTerminal.valuationSubtitle: First quantitative layer for an executive read of the asset.
AssetTerminal.fundamentalsSubtitle: Trailing-twelve-month metrics from a professional feed — complements the live quote snapshot.
AssetTerminal.sessionSubtitle: Open, previous close, day range, volume and distance from 52-week highs/lows.
AssetTerminal.returnsSubtitle: Computed on the same history window as the chart (up to ~10 years when the source allows).
AssetTerminal.ratiosSubtitle: Beta, margins, dividends and capital structure when published in the detailed quote.
AssetTerminal.calendarSubtitle: First vs last close of each year in the series — not official total return.
AssetTerminal.riskSubtitle: Maximum drawdown and annualized volatility implied from daily closes.
AssetTerminal.dividendsSubtitle: Payment history, trailing 12-month yield and upcoming distributions from market data.
AssetTerminal.dividendsEmpty: No distribution history published for this symbol from the current source.
AssetTerminal.dividendsDisclaimer: Past distributions do not guarantee future payouts. Confirm dates with the company and your broker before trading.
AssetTerminal.dividendsByYearSubtitle: Total distributions paid per calendar year (filterable).
AssetTerminal.dividendsYieldByYearSubtitle: Year distributions ÷ last close of that year (approx.).
AssetTerminal.dividendsYieldEmpty: Annual yield unavailable — missing price or distributions in window.
AssetTerminal.dividendsFilterEmpty: No distributions of this type in the window.
AssetTerminal.statementsSubtitle: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow on the latest annual row available from the feed — executive read, not a substitute for audited filings.
AssetTerminal.statementsDisclaimer: Figures reflect what the company reported to the data vendor. Filing lag, restatements and FX effects can change the picture. PRONUXFIN does not audit these numbers and does not provide investment advice.
AssetTerminal.termsSubtitle: What the company does, sector framing, market peers and reads derived from the price curve — not a substitute for financial statements or regulatory filings.
AssetTerminal.termsPeersDisclaimer: Tickers often correlated or in the same sector per the data feed. They are not subsidiaries, affiliates or corporate group members.
AssetTerminal.termsPeersEmpty: No peer list returned for this symbol from the external feed.
AssetTerminal.termsSubsidiariesNote: Branches, subsidiaries and full corporate group structure usually require regulatory filings (SEC, CVM, etc.) or premium databases. Here we only show what the public feed returns reliably.
AssetTerminal.termsCalendarTitle: Years on the price curve (calendar view)
AssetTerminal.termsBestYear: Strongest calendar year in the window
AssetTerminal.termsWorstYear: Weakest calendar year in the window
AssetTerminal.termsNegativeYearsNone: No calendar year with a net decline in the available interval.
AssetTerminal.termsVolumeYearsTitle: Heaviest exchange turnover (volume summed by calendar year)
AssetTerminal.termsHistoryLimited: The series spans fewer than ~13 months of sessions; multi-year reads will change as history grows.
AssetTerminal.termsVolumePartial: Some sessions arrived without volume from the feed; the volume ranking is approximate.
AssetTerminal.termsCalendarDisclaimer: Annual return uses the first and last available closes of each calendar year in the series. It is not official total return; dividends only appear if already embedded in the feed’s adjusted price.
AssetTerminal.movesSubtitle: Most relevant moves in the recent window plus annual range position.
AssetTerminal.watchlistError: Could not update your watchlist right now.
AssetTerminal.portfolioPositionTitle: Your simulated position in this asset
AssetTerminal.portfolioPositionDisclaimer: P&L based on the latest available quote — not a brokerage account.
AssetTerminal.newsSubtitle: Editorial read connected to the asset inside the PRONUXFIN desk.
AssetTerminal.newsEmpty: We have not yet identified headlines with strong enough affinity to this asset. Coverage will expand in the next layers.

AssetTerminal.assistantLead: Use the assistant to discuss scenario, risk, triggers and institutional framing for {symbol} inside your account.
